title: Psalms Chapter 14 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 14 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 14 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 14.

questions.question: In Psalms 14, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God.
The LORD looked down from heaven
questions.correctAnswer: The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God.
questions.explanation: This is the first statement in the chapter as seen in Psalms 14:1.

questions.question: What has the fool said in his heart according to Psalms 14?
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:1 states that the fool hath said in his heart, 'There is no God.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 14, what are the actions of the corrupt?
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:1 indicates that the corrupt 'have done abominable works.'

questions.question: What does the LORD do in Psalms 14?
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:2 says, 'The LORD looked down from heaven upon the children of men.'

questions.question: Who does the LORD look down upon in Psalms 14?
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:2 states that the LORD looked down upon 'the children of men.'

questions.question: What is the purpose of the LORD looking down from heaven?
options: To see if there were any that did understand.
questions.correctAnswer: To see if there were any that did understand.
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:2 explains that He looked down 'to see if there were any that did understand.'

questions.question: What has happened to all people according to Psalms 14?
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:3 states, 'They are all gone aside.'

questions.question: What description is given of the people in Psalms 14?
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:3 says that 'they are all together become filthy.'

questions.question: How many people does Psalms 14 claim doeth good?
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:3 states, 'there is none that doeth good, no, not one.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 14, are there any who seek God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:3 infers that there is none who doeth good, implying that none seek God.

questions.question: According to Psalms 14, who is described as a fool?
options: The one who says there is no God.
questions.correctAnswer: The one who says there is no God.
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:1 identifies the fool as one who says in his heart, 'There is no God.'

questions.question: Is it true that the fool is described as corrupt in Psalms 14?
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:1 states that the fool 'are corrupt.'

questions.question: Is it true that the LORD seeks good people according to Psalms 14?
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:2 indicates that the LORD looked to see if there were any that did understand and seek God.

questions.question: Is it false that Psalms 14 claims that some people do good?
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:3 explicitly states that 'there is none that doeth good, no, not one.'

questions.question: Is it false that the LORD is indifferent to the actions of men according to Psalms 14?
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:2 shows that the LORD looked down to see the actions of men, indicating His concern.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 14 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 14 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What do the workers of iniquity do to my people according to Psalms 14:4?
options: They eat them as they eat bread
questions.correctAnswer: They eat them as they eat bread
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 14:4 states that the workers of iniquity eat up my people as they eat bread.

questions.question: What does Psalms 14:5 promise will happen if someone does what Psalms 14:4 commands?
options: They will be in great fear
questions.correctAnswer: They will be in great fear
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 14:5 mentions that there were they in great fear, linking it to the actions of the workers of iniquity in verse 4.

questions.question: According to Psalms 14:4, what do the workers of iniquity fail to do?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 14:4 asks rhetorically if the workers of iniquity have knowledge, for they do not call upon the LORD.

questions.question: What does Psalms 14:6 say about the counsel of the poor?
options: It is honored by the rich
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 14:6 states that they have shamed the counsel of the poor, indicating a disregard for their wisdom.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the righteous and God according to Psalms 14:5?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 14:5 states that God is in the generation of the righteous, implying His presence and support.

questions.question: According to Psalms 14:1, what does the fool say in his heart?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 14:1 explicitly states that the fool hath said in his heart, 'There is no God.'

questions.question: What is the condition of the workers of iniquity as described in Psalms 14:1?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 14:1 states that the workers of iniquity are corrupt and have done abominable works.

questions.question: According to Psalms 14:2, what does the LORD look for among the children of men?
options: Those who understand and seek God
questions.correctAnswer: Those who understand and seek God
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 14:2 states that the LORD looked down to see if there were any that did understand and seek God.

questions.question: What is indicated about the state of humanity in Psalms 14:3?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 14:3 indicates that all have gone aside and are altogether become filthy.

questions.question: What role does the LORD play for the poor according to Psalms 14:6?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 14:6 states that the LORD is a refuge for the poor, indicating His protective nature.

questions.question: Those who do not call upon the LORD are referred to as what in Psalms 14:4?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 14:4 identifies those who do not call upon the LORD as the workers of iniquity.

questions.question: The statement 'There is none that doeth good' is found in which verse?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 14:1 states that there is none that doeth good.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 14:5, God is in the generation of the righteous.
questions.explanation: This is true as Psalms 14:5 explicitly states that God is in the generation of the righteous.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 14:6 states that the poor have no refuge.
questions.explanation: This is false because Psalms 14:6 states that the LORD is a refuge for the poor.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 14:3 indicates that there are some who do good.
questions.explanation: This is false as Psalms 14:3 states that there is none that doeth good.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 14 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 14.

questions.question: In Psalms 14:7, what is described as coming out of Zion?
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:7 explicitly states, 'Oh that the salvation of Israel were come out of Zion!' indicating salvation as the key theme.

questions.question: According to Psalms 14:7, what event causes Jacob to rejoice and Israel to be glad?
options: When the LORD bringeth back the captivity of his people
When enemies are defeated by the sword
When the law is given on Mount Sinai
questions.correctAnswer: When the LORD bringeth back the captivity of his people
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:7 states that 'when the LORD bringeth back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.'

questions.question: What does the phrase 'bringeth back the captivity of his people' in Psalms 14:7 foreshadow in Israel's history?
options: The destruction of Jerusalem by Assyria
questions.explanation: The phrase in Psalms 14:7 foreshadows the historical event of the Israelites returning from Babylonian captivity, a major restoration theme in the Old Testament.

questions.question: Which of the following best captures the mood expressed in Psalms 14:7 concerning Israel's future?
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:7 concludes with 'Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad,' expressing hopeful rejoicing for future salvation.

questions.question: In Psalms 14:7, 'Jacob' and 'Israel' are used together. What literary purpose does this serve?
options: Reference to two different historical periods
questions.explanation: The terms 'Jacob' and 'Israel' in Psalms 14:7 are parallel names for the same people, used to emphasize the nation as a whole.

questions.question: What theological hope is expressed in the final verse of Psalms 14?
options: God’s salvation and restoration of Israel
The establishment of a new temple
questions.correctAnswer: God’s salvation and restoration of Israel
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:7 expresses hope for salvation and restoration: 'Oh that the salvation of Israel were come out of Zion!'

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'yeshuah' (יְשׁוּעָה) in Psalms 14:7 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'yeshuah' in Psalms 14:7 means 'salvation,' referring to deliverance or rescue.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Psalms 14:7 with the phrases 'Jacob shall rejoice' and 'Israel shall be glad'?
questions.explanation: The pairs 'Jacob shall rejoice' and 'Israel shall be glad' in Psalms 14:7 are examples of synonymous parallelism, common in Hebrew poetry.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God bringing back His people’s captivity as seen in Psalms 14:7?
questions.explanation: Luke 1:68-69 speaks of God visiting and redeeming His people, fulfilling the hope of restoration expressed in Psalms 14:7.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage closely connects to the theme of Israel’s salvation and restoration in Psalms 14:7?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 52:7 speaks of beautiful feet bringing good news of peace and salvation to Zion, echoing the salvation theme in Psalms 14:7.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Psalms 14:7 in the chapter?
options: Ye have shamed the counsel of the poor, because the LORD is his refuge.
There were they in great fear: for God is in the generation of the righteous.
Have all the workers of iniquity no knowledge?
The LORD looked down from heaven upon the children of men.
questions.correctAnswer: Ye have shamed the counsel of the poor, because the LORD is his refuge.
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:6 immediately precedes 14:7 and states, 'Ye have shamed the counsel of the poor, because the LORD is his refuge.'

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'bringeth back the captivity' in Psalms 14:7 from a typological perspective?
options: It foreshadows Christ’s spiritual deliverance of believers.
It refers only to literal historical events without typology.
It symbolizes the exile of the fallen angels.
It predicts the destruction of the temple in AD 70.
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Christ’s spiritual deliverance of believers.
questions.explanation: Typologically, the return from captivity in Psalms 14:7 points to Christ’s ultimate spiritual deliverance and restoration of God’s people.

questions.question: Which rhetorical device is found in Psalms 14:1 with the phrase 'The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God'?
questions.explanation: The statement in Psalms 14:1 is ironic because it describes the fool’s denial of God as folly, contrasting belief and wisdom.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 14:7 expresses a confident expectation of God’s salvation coming from Zion.
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:7 explicitly states a hope and expectation for the salvation of Israel to come from Zion.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 14:7 states that Israel’s captivity is permanent and without hope of restoration.
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:7 expresses hope that the LORD will bring back the captivity of His people, indicating restoration is expected.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 14 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 14 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 14:1 teach about human sin?
options: Human beings are inherently corrupt and deny God's existence.
Humanity is essentially good but sometimes errs.
Sin is only external disobedience, not internal denial.
Only a few humans reject God outright.
questions.correctAnswer: Human beings are inherently corrupt and deny God's existence.
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:1 states that 'The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God. They are corrupt, they have done abominable works...' showing human sinfulness as both corrupt and involving denial of God.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 14:2 teach about God's knowledge and providence?
options: God is omniscient and actively seeks those who understand and seek Him.
God is indifferent to human understanding and seeking.
God only passively observes human affairs.
God does not intervene in human morality.
questions.correctAnswer: God is omniscient and actively seeks those who understand and seek Him.
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:2 says, 'The LORD looked down from heaven... to see if there were any that did understand, and seek God,' indicating God's active knowledge and providence.

questions.question: What doctrine about universal human depravity is taught in Psalms 14:3?
options: All humans have sinned and there is none who does good.
Some humans are naturally righteous without God's help.
Human depravity is limited to certain groups.
questions.correctAnswer: All humans have sinned and there is none who does good.
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:3 explicitly states, 'They are all gone aside... no, not one,' teaching universal human depravity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 14:2 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 shows God looking down from heaven to see if any seek Him, demonstrating His omniscience—complete knowledge of human hearts.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 14:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Psalms 14:5 says 'God is in the generation of the righteous,' showing God's immanence—His presence among His people.

questions.question: How does Psalms 14 connect to New Testament teachings on salvation?
options: It anticipates the need for divine salvation due to universal sinfulness.
It teaches salvation by works alone.
It denies the necessity of repentance.
It focuses only on Old Testament sacrificial systems.
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the need for divine salvation due to universal sinfulness.
questions.explanation: The chapter's emphasis on no one doing good (v.3) anticipates the New Testament doctrine of salvation by grace through faith because of universal sinfulness (e.g., Romans 3:10-12).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme is prepared by Psalms 14:7?
options: The future restoration of Israel and the joy of redemption.
The final judgment of the wicked.
The establishment of the Davidic monarchy.
questions.correctAnswer: The future restoration of Israel and the joy of redemption.
questions.explanation: Verse 7 expresses longing for salvation from Zion and the return of captivity, which points forward to messianic restoration themes fulfilled in Christ.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 1 and 3 teach about human sinfulness?
options: All humans are corrupt and none do good.
Only some humans deny God and sin.
Sin is external, not internal denial of God.
questions.correctAnswer: All humans are corrupt and none do good.
questions.explanation: Verses 1 and 3 together emphasize that fools deny God and all have become corrupt with none doing good, teaching total depravity.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 4 and 6 teach about God’s justice and protection?
options: God protects the poor and punishes workers of iniquity.
God favors the wealthy and ignores the poor.
questions.correctAnswer: God protects the poor and punishes workers of iniquity.
questions.explanation: Verse 4 addresses workers of iniquity who oppress God's people, and verse 6 states the LORD is refuge for the poor, teaching God's justice and protection.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 5 and 7 teach about the righteous community and eschatological hope?
options: God dwells with the righteous and will restore Israel in the last days.
The righteous will be abandoned and Israel destroyed forever.
God only cares for individuals, not communities.
The hope of Israel is based solely on political power.
questions.correctAnswer: God dwells with the righteous and will restore Israel in the last days.
questions.explanation: Verse 5 affirms God is in the generation of the righteous, and verse 7 expresses hope for Israel's salvation and restoration, indicating eschatological hope.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Psalms 14:1-3 teaches that God’s existence cannot be known due to human corruption. What does Psalms 14:1-3 actually teach?
options: It teaches that denial of God is folly and all are corrupt, not that God's existence is unknowable.
It supports agnosticism about God's existence.
It claims God does not care about human sin.
It denies any moral consequences for rejecting God.
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that denial of God is folly and all are corrupt, not that God's existence is unknowable.
questions.explanation: Verses 1-3 describe the fool who denies God and the universal corruption of mankind, emphasizing folly and sin rather than agnosticism.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 14:4 teach about the knowledge of workers of iniquity concerning God?
options: Workers of iniquity lack true knowledge of God and fail to call upon Him.
Workers of iniquity have perfect knowledge of God but reject Him.
Workers of iniquity do not exist in reality.
Workers of iniquity secretly worship God.
questions.correctAnswer: Workers of iniquity lack true knowledge of God and fail to call upon Him.
questions.explanation: Verse 4 questions if workers of iniquity have knowledge and notes they do not call upon the LORD, indicating ignorance or rejection of God.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 14:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 7's hope for salvation and restoration 'when the LORD bringeth back the captivity' shows God's faithfulness to His covenant promises.

questions.question: How do Psalms 14:1 and 14:4 together deepen understanding of human sin and divine judgment?
options: Humans are corrupt fools denying God, and workers of iniquity lack knowledge and oppress God’s people, incurring judgment.
Humans are basically good, and workers of iniquity are misunderstood.
Humans sin only occasionally, and God does not judge.
Workers of iniquity secretly honor God.
questions.correctAnswer: Humans are corrupt fools denying God, and workers of iniquity lack knowledge and oppress God’s people, incurring judgment.
questions.explanation: Verse 1 shows fools deny God and are corrupt; verse 4 shows workers of iniquity oppress God's people and lack knowledge, illustrating sin deserving judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 14:6 teach about God's protection of the marginalized?
options: The LORD is a refuge for the poor and defends their counsel.
The poor are abandoned by God.
God favors only the rich in society.
The counsel of the poor is worthless before God.
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD is a refuge for the poor and defends their counsel.
questions.explanation: Verse 6 states ‘because the LORD is his refuge,’ showing God's protective care for the poor and their counsel.
